summary: The record's runtime claims survive the adversarial check. HF API sizes, config-derived KV math (147,456 B/token BF16; vLLM FP8 build pool 5.0005e9 B gives ~33.9k BF16-KV / ~67.8k FP8-KV tokens; INT4 ~56.5k/113k; llama.cpp Q8_0+q8_0 KV at 64k = 13.7 GiB), the deepseek_v3 parser RuntimeError, missing tool tokens, the vLLM docs marking R1 tools unsupported, and the llama.cpp doc and template claims are all confirmed. Two corrections. (1) In v0.33.0, '--quantization fp8' on a BF16 checkpoint is deprecated: get_quant_config logs a warning and switches to fp8_per_tensor (Fp8Config itself raises ValueError for online use), so the command should say '--quantization fp8_per_tensor'. Online FP8 builds each layer from the meta device as it loads, so peak load memory is not a risk. (2) '--kv-cache-dtype fp8' does not run on FlashAttention 2 on sm_120: flash_attn_supports_kv_cache_dtype allows FP8 only on sm90 (FA3/FA4) and sm100 (FA4), so vLLM falls back to FlashInfer (order FLASH_ATTN, FLASHINFER, TRITON_ATTN). Expect a possible FlashInfer first-start compile. The 64k setting leaves only ~3% headroom. Ollama's refusal of tools for deepseek-r1:8b moves from inferred to source-backed: the 8b template has no Tools variable, and server/images.go only grants the tools capability when the template contains 'tools' or 'tool_call'. llama.cpp b12418 has no dedicated R1 tool handler in chat.cpp and relies on the auto-parser, so whether it recognises R1's tool-call text is still untraced. Verdict 'unsuitable for OpenCode' holds. Best realistic configuration: unsloth Q8_0 on llama.cpp, 64k context, q8_0 KV, --jinja, with tool calls mechanically possible but unproven. Gaps: Artificial Analysis scores not re-checked; INT4 AutoRound Marlin path on sm_120 not checked; no end-to-end tool-call run.

verdicts.claim: Weight sizes: official BF16 16.38 GB (15.26 GiB); JamAndTea FP8 9.43 GB; Intel INT4 6.10 GB; unsloth/bartowski Q8_0 8.71 GB, Q6_K 6.73, Q4_K_M 5.03, BF16 16.39 GB
Architecture Qwen3ForCausalLM, 36 full-attention layers, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128, max_position_embeddings 131072 via YaRN x4 over 32768; KV 147,456 B/token BF16
vLLM FP8 budget: pool 4.66 GiB, ~33.9k BF16-KV / ~67.9k FP8-KV tokens; INT4 ~56.5k / ~113k
verdicts.correction: Recomputed: 15,727,591,424 - 9,438,581,960 - 1,288,490,189 = 5,000,519,275 B, giving 33,912 (BF16 KV) and 67,823 (FP8 KV) tokens, not 67,866. --max-model-len 65536 has only ~3% headroom over a 1.2 GiB reserve estimate.

verdicts.claim: Serve command uses '--quantization fp8' for online dynamic FP8 on v0.33.0
verdicts.correction: In v0.33.0, Fp8Config raises ValueError for online use ('no longer supports online quantization. Please use --quantization fp8_per_tensor'). get_quant_config catches '--quantization fp8' on a checkpoint without a quant config, logs a deprecation warning and switches to fp8_per_tensor, so it still starts. Use '--quantization fp8_per_tensor'. Online FP8 (online/fp8.py, uses_meta_device=True, layerwise processing) materializes each layer as it loads, so peak load memory is not a concern.

verdicts.claim: Attention on sm_120 is FlashAttention 2 (implied to apply with --kv-cache-dtype fp8)
verdicts.correction: flash_attn_supports_kv_cache_dtype returns True for FP8 only on sm90 (FA3/FA4) or sm100 (FA4), not sm_120. With FP8 KV, the backend order (cuda.py: FLASH_ATTN, FLASHINFER, TRITON_ATTN) selects FlashInfer, which lists fp8 KV support. Expect a possible FlashInfer compile on first start. BF16 KV stays on FA2.

verdicts.claim: llama.cpp: qwen3 arch supported, latest release b12419; docs say DeepSeek R1 WIP/reluctant; llama-cpp-deepseek-r1.jinja ships in models/templates; chat.cpp warns about templates that do not describe tools
unsloth GGUF embedded template renders tools (sglang R1 tool template); bartowski template does not
verdicts.correction: In b12418, chat.cpp has no dedicated DeepSeek R1 tool-call handler (only V3.2/V4/V4.1). Parsing R1's multi-token tool-call text depends on the generic auto-parser (chat-auto-parser-*.cpp), which was not traced, so llama.cpp tool calling stays mechanically possible but unproven.

verdicts.claim: llama.cpp VRAM plan: Q8_0 + q8_0 KV at 65536 = 13.7 GiB; Q8_0 + f16 KV = 17.9 GiB does not fit; Q4_K_M + q8_0 KV at 131072 = 15.0 GiB
Ollama deepseek-r1:8b template has no .Tools; tool requests probably refused (inferred)
verdicts.correction: Now source-backed: template blob sha256:c5ad996bda6e (556 B) has no Tools variable, and images.go grants the tools capability only if the template contains 'tools' or 'tool_call', so tool requests fail with a 'does not support tools' error. Model blob 5,225,373,760 B. Ollama v0.40.17-rc0 is a pre-release.
